vam:O88110.summary: This small ivory casket is carved on every side with the story of Christ's Passion and Resurrection: the Last Supper on the front, Christ before Herod and the Betrayal on the back, the Agony in the Garden and the Crucifixion on the ends, and on the lid the holy women at the tomb and the Harrowing of Hell. The front, shown here, presents the apostles gathered at a long table with Christ, framed by acanthus borders and later gilt-metal straps.
facts: Its small size and the Last Supper placed on the front suggest, according to the V&A, that it was made as a Eucharistic vessel to hold the unconsecrated host.
The gilt-metal mounts date from about the 12th century, while the hinges and lock are modern.
It belongs to a group of ivories probably from the same workshop, including the V&A's Passion plaque 1-1872 and a panel in Essen; it was in the Farrer collection, sold at Christie's on 13 June 1866.
